newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares up, but off intra-day high.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares up, but off intra-day high.

text.p: Shanghai B shares closed down on Tuesday on strong performance by shares related to the Pudong development zone, but off their intra-day year-high of 55.097 points due to profit-taking in the afternoon, brokers said.
The index rose 1.104 points or 2.10 percent to 53.766 points, on volume of 36.4 million shares worth $15.7 million. Of 42 shares, 41 traded, with 19 up, seven flat and 15 down.

Brokers said the strong performance of Pudong shares had boosted follow-up buying, but profit-taking selling later in the session prevented the market from rising further with Shenzhen B shares falling back after a strong surge in the morning.
"The market met strong resistance around 54-55 points which institutions had tried to breach by buying index-weight stocks," one broker said.
"Domestic individual investors have come in to buy, which is not permitted according to the rules," a second broker said. "The attitudes of the authorities will decide the market directions."
"The market is likely to consolidate between 52-54 points tomorrow to digest heavy profit-taking counters after sharp gains in the past few days," a third broker said.

Newcomer Huangshan Tourism was the star on active speculative buying, but follow-up buying in the afternoon would have been risky at current prices, brokers said. It surged 0.062 or 19.37 percent to $0.382 on volume of 4.1 million shares.

Market giant Shanghai Tyre Rubber followed on window-dressing buying by an institution which holds big positions in it, brokers said. It rose $0.032 or 8.46 percent to $0.410 on volume of 1.1 million shares.
The market barometer Shangahai Lujiazui was the third winner, rising $0.066 or 6.40 percent to $1.096 on volume of $3.4 million.
Shanghai A shares fell on cautious market sentiment with concerns about possible intervention from Beijing, brokers said.

The A index lost 10.168 points or 0.99 percent to 1015.592 points, on volume of 488.6 million shares worth 5.0 billion yuan. The SSE 30 Blue-Chip index dropped 31.914 points or 1.29 percent to 2435.791 points.

Shanghai Shenhua Electronics was the biggest loser after an institution announced it had increased its holdings in the company, falling 1.58 yuan or 6.74 percent to 21.85 yuan on volume of 8.1 million shares.
